lso-delivery.text:
Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of a prefabricated Lumbar-Sacral Orthosis (LSO) with sagittal-coronal rigid panels from Trend for {Indication: Acute Lumbar Disc Herniation with Radiculopathy / Compression Fracture Lumbar/ Lumbar Spinal Stenosis / Spondylolisthesis (Grade I/II) / Post-Operative Lumbar Fusion or Discectomy / Severe Mechanical Low Back Pain / Lumbar Facet Syndrome}.

Clinical Context & Examination:
Patient presents with severe lumbosacral pain, trunk muscular guarding, and mechanical instability that restricts spinal range of motion and limits sitting, standing, and walking endurance.

Fitting, Anatomical Contouring & Compression Mechanism:
Patient's abdominal circumference was measured at [Circumference]. He/she was fit with a size {Size: 0/1/1.5/2/2.5/3/3.5/4/4.5/5/5.5} LSO. Rigid anterior panel (extending from symphysis pubis to xiphoid) and rigid posterior panel (extending from sacrococcygeal junction to T9 vertebra) with lateral panels were heat-contoured to match the patient's lordotic curvature. The integrated mechanical pulley system was engaged to achieve rigid circumferential intracavitary compression. Fit verified in sitting, standing, and bending positions; motion restriction confirmed.

Medical Necessity:
The sagittal-coronal LSO is reasonable and medically necessary to restrict spinal motion in the sagittal and coronal planes (L1–L5/S1), increase intracavitary abdominal pressure to offload axial compressive forces from the intervertebral discs, stabilize the lumbar vertebrae, and relieve severe low back pain during daily activities.

Patient Education & Care:
He/she was instructed on donning/doffing over a cotton t-shirt, pulley pull-tab adjustment, posture ergonomics during transfers, and skin monitoring. Verbal/written instructions provided; follow-up PRN.
lso-delivery.title: LSO Delivery

lumbar-corset.text:
Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of a sagittal control Lumbar-Sacral Corset with rigid posterior stays from Ezwrap for {Indication: Post-Op Spinal Cord Stimulator Lead Stabilization / Acute Lumbosacral Muscle Strain / Chronic Mechanical Low Back Pain / Lumbar Spondylosis without radiculopathy}.

Clinical Context:
{Clinical Presentation: Patient presents pre-op installation of spinal cord stimulator (SCS) placement requiring lumbar immobilization to prevent lead migration and reduce post-surgical pain / Patient exhibits severe lumbosacral muscle spasm, postural guarding, and mechanical low back pain}.

Fitting & Compression Verification:
He/she was fit with a size {Size: XXS/XSmall/Small/Med/Large/XL/2XL/3XL/4XL} elastic/canvas lumbar corset. Posterior contoured rigid aluminum stays were customized to patient's anatomical lordosis (extending from sacrococcygeal junction to T9). Dual bilateral elastic compression pull-straps were tensioned to generate uniform intracavitary abdominal compression and support the paraspinal musculature.

Medical Necessity:
The lumbar corset orthosis is reasonable and medically necessary to {Medical Necessity: restrict lumbar motion and prevent lead displacement following spinal cord stimulator placement / restrict painful sagittal flexion, increase intra-abdominal pressure, and relieve mechanical low back strain}.

Patient Education:
Instructed on proper anterior fastening, wearing over a clean barrier shirt, progressive wear schedule, and proper body mechanics. {Precautions: Emphasized spine-neutral precautions (no bending, lifting, or twisting) to protect SCS lead positioning / Emphasized standard spine-neutral lifting body mechanics}. Follow-up PRN.
lumbar-corset.title: Lumbar Corset

custom-1787583412902.title: Diabetic shoe/Toe filler evaluation
custom-1787583412902.text:
Patient presents to the North/South office for clinical evaluation, anatomical measurement, and volumetric impressions for a custom Left/Right/Bilateral partial foot prosthesis with toe filler (L5000), therapeutic diabetic depth footwear (A5500 x 2), and multi-density total contact inserts (A5513). he/she is under active diabetic management by his/her certifying physician. Patient arrived {Ambulatory state: ambulating unaided / ambulating with cane / ambulating with walker / in wheelchair}.

Qualifying Medical History & Rationale:
Patient has a documented history of Diabetes Mellitus and presents with: Left/Right {Amputation History: partial foot amputation / Transmetatarsal amputation (TMA) / Lisfranc amputation / Chopart amputation / Great toe amputation with ray resection / Multi-digit amputation / Bilateral partial foot amputations}. Medical necessity is established to provide a custom partial foot prosthesis with rigid/flexible toe filler to replace missing skeletal leverage, fill footwear void, prevent forward sliding/shear within the shoe, protect the residual limb from skin breakdown, and restore functional rollover during the stance phase of gait.

Physical Examination & Biomechanical Assessment:

Residual Limb & Skin Integrity: Skin is {Skin Status: completely intact without lesions / fully healed surgical site / healed with localized hyperkeratosis / adherent distal scar tissue}. {Callus: No hyperkeratotic callus noted. / Callus noted on Left 1st Met Head. / Callus noted on Right 1st Met Head. / Callus noted on Bilateral 1st Met Heads. / Callus noted on Left 2nd-4th Met Heads. / Callus noted on Right 2nd-4th Met Heads. / Callus noted on Bilateral 2nd-4th Met Heads. / Callus noted on Left 5th Met Head. / Callus noted on Right 5th Met Head. / Callus noted on Bilateral 5th Met Heads. / Callus noted on Left Plantar Heel. / Callus noted on Right Plantar Heel. / Callus noted on Bilateral Plantar Heels.}
{+ Prior Ulcer Site: Healed prior ulcer site noted on [Prior Ulcer Location].}
No active open ulcerations, drainage, or signs of acute infection noted.

Structural Assessment & Contralateral Foot: Physical examination reveals {Contralateral Deformities: intact contralateral foot with no rigid deformities / hallux valgus (bunions) / hammer or claw toes / Charcot arthropathy / severe pes planus / prominent metatarsal heads / bilateral amputation sites}.

Neurological Assessment: Sensation testing demonstrates {Sensation: Loss of Protective Sensation / Loss of protective sensation distally but intact proximal to mets / Loss of protective sensation but intact proximal to ankle / intact protective sensation}.

Foot Sizing, Custom Impressions & Device Selection:

Brannock Sizing (Weight-Bearing): Determined shoe size: {Shoe Size: 5 / 5.5 / 6 / 6.5 / 7 / 7.5 / 8 / 8.5 / 9 / 9.5 / 10 / 10.5 / 11 / 11.5 / 12 / 12.5 / 13 / 14 / 15} / Width: {Shoe Width: M / W / XW / XXW}.

Therapeutic Footwear Selected: {Brand: Anodyne / Dr. Comfort / Orthofeet / Apex / Mt. Emey} — Size: {Shoe Size: 5 / 5.5 / 6 / 6.5 / 7 / 7.5 / 8 / 8.5 / 9 / 9.5 / 10 / 10.5 / 11 / 11.5 / 12 / 12.5 / 13 / 14 / 15} / Width: {Shoe Width: M / W / XW / XXW}.

Impressions Obtained: Direct 3D volumetric impressions / foam impression boxes taken today of bilateral feet for custom multi-density insert fabrication. The custom insert incorporates a longitudinal arch support and Left/Right custom toe filler (L5000) molded to match the anatomical contour of the residual limb.

Plan & Patient Education:

Order Placed: HCPCS A5500 x 2 (Therapeutic depth shoes), HCPCS L5000 Left/Right (Partial foot prosthesis with toe filler), and HCPCS A5513 (Custom-molded multi-density inserts).

Next Steps: Patient will return for prosthetic delivery, shoe fitting, total contact pressure check, and dynamic gait trial upon completion of custom fabrication.

Education Provided: Patient was educated on a progressive break-in schedule (1–2 hours daily), daily visual skin checks using a mirror, diabetic seamless socks, and immediate reporting of any erythema lasting >20 minutes. {+ Caregiver Present: Caregiver was present and instructed on daily residual limb inspection and footwear safety.}

Follow-up scheduled in {Follow-up: 3-4 weeks for custom fitting and delivery / PRN upon order arrival}.

custom-1787665453088.title: Generic orthosis adjustment
custom-1787665453088.text:
Patient presented to the North/South clinic for evaluation, clinical assessment, and adjustment/repair of his/her existing Left/Right {Device Type: Walking Boot/Ankle-Foot Orthosis (AFO) / Knee Orthosis (KO) / Lumbar-Sacral Orthosis (LSO) / Cervical Collar / Form Foot Orthotics / Custom Foot Orthotics/ Arch Rivals / Abduction Sling/ Wrist-Hand Orthosis (WHO) / Knee-Ankle-Foot Orthosis (KAFO)}.

Subjective Complaints & Clinical History:
Patient reports {Issue: localized pressure and rubbing / straps losing adherence and failing to maintain compression / device migration during activity / skin redness over bony prominence / edge impingement during sitting/ambulation / anatomical volume changes affecting fit}. Adjustments are medically necessary to eliminate skin irritation, restore proper anatomical alignment, ensure structural integrity, and maintain prescribed joint stabilization/offloading during daily functional activities.

Objective Assessment & Adjustments Performed:
Inspection of Existing Device: Evaluation of device reveals {Device Status: worn/delaminated hook-and-loop straps / localized point pressure over bony prominence / edge digging / minor structural fatigue / padding compression}.

Modifications Performed Today:
{Modification: Heat flared and remolded thermoplastic trimlines to relieve focal pressure / Replaced worn Velcro straps and re-anchored tension closures / Added relief padding over bony prominence / Realigned and contoured metal uprights / Ground down and smoothed plastic edge impingements / Added posting/wedging to optimize biomechanical alignment / Replaced worn closure hardware and re-tensioned pulleys}.

Labor & Service Time: Repair and clinical adjustment completed requiring {Labor Units: 1 unit (15 min) / 2 units (30 min) / 3 units (45 min) / 4 units (60 min)} of custom bench modification and refitting labor (HCPCS L4205).
{+ Replacement Straps/Materials: Replacement materials and closures installed to restore original function.}

Outcome & Patient Verification:
Trial & Fit Check: Device was re-donned; verified intimate total contact, restored structural security, and complete relief of prior pressure areas with zero active impingement during functional trials.

Skin & Safety Assessment: Visual skin inspection after weight-bearing/motion trial confirmed no persistent erythema or tissue compromise.

Patient Education: Patient was re-instructed on proper strap tensioning, donning alignment, and continued daily skin checks. {+ Caregiver Present: Caregiver was present and reviewed on adjusted fit and application.}

Patient verbalized significant improvement in comfort and stability. Device returned in safe working order. Follow-up PRN.

afo-carbon-del.title: AFO/Carbon Delivery
afo-carbon-del.text:
Patient was seen at the North/South location for fitting and delivery of a Left/Right energy-storing carbon fiber Ankle-Foot Orthosis {HCPCS Code: L1932 (Custom Fitted Carbon Fiber) / L1951 (Spiral Prefab Custom Fitted) / L1945 (Custom Molded Rigid Anterior Tibial Section)}).

Subjective & Clinical Rationale:
Patient presents with Left/Right lower extremity weakness secondary to {Indication: Drop Foot secondary to Peroneal Nerve Palsy / Post-Stroke Hemiplegia / Lumbar Radiculopathy (L4/L5) / Multiple Sclerosis / Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury / Charcot-Marie-Tooth / Severe Dorsiflexion Weakness}. The carbon fiber AFO is medically necessary and reasonable to provide dynamic energy return, assist swing-phase toe clearance, prevent foot drop tripping falls, control sagittal plane progression, and stabilize the ankle complex during community ambulation.

Biomechanical Specifications & In-Office Modifications:

Device Characteristics: Lightweight prepreg carbon fiber composite strut with {Strut Design: dynamic posterior strut / anterior lateral strut / rigid anterior tibial cuff / full-length dynamic footplate / sulcus-length flexible footplate}.

Custom Modifications & Fit:

Proximal calf/tibial cuff interface aligned to anatomical contours with soft padding lining (L2820).

Footplate positioned within patient’s standard footwear; minor footplate adjustments and insole seating completed to ensure intimate contact without edge digging or forefoot impingement.

Proximal hook-and-loop closure tensioned securely to maintain uncompromised tibial positioning without proximal fibular head or peroneal nerve pressure.
{+ Added Soft Interface: Soft interface lining added to rigid carbon section for bony prominence relief.}

Functional Assessment & Patient Education:

Gait Evaluation: Dynamic gait analysis demonstrated immediate restoration of swing-phase dorsiflexion clearance, smooth heel strike to toe-off energy transfer, elimination of steppage gait / hip hiking, and improved step symmetry across uneven clinic surfaces.

Donning / Doffing: Patient was educated on proper shoe insertion, donning techniques, and strap tensioning. he/she independently and accurately applied the device.

Care & Safety Protocols: Patient was instructed on a progressive break-in schedule (increasing 1–2 hours daily), wearing over a clean moisture-wicking sock, footwear heel-height restrictions, and daily visual skin inspection over the anterior tibia, malleoli, and plantar surface. {+ Caregiver Present: Caregiver was present and instructed on proper application and skin safety.}

All questions were answered, and the patient verbalized complete understanding. Device delivered in proper working order. Follow-up scheduled in {Follow-up: 2 weeks / 4 weeks / PRN}.

afo-carbon-eval.title: AFO/Carbon Evaluation
afo-carbon-eval.text:
Patient presents at North/South office for evaluation of progressive gait instability, lower extremity weakness, and frequent tripping/falls impacting daily activities. He/She has been diagnosed with foot drop Left/Right due to {Diagnosis: Spinal stenosis/Muscular Dystrophy/Peripheral Neuropathy/Post-Stroke Hemiplegia/Multiple Sclerosis/Charcot-Marie-Tooth/CP}. Patient experiences persistent foot drop during the swing phase of gait and muscle fatigue after walking short distances. Current off-the-shelf bracing or lack of bracing provides inadequate energy return and insufficient stability to control dynamic gait deviations. Ambulation is limited to {Ambulation Distance: <100 feet/100-300 feet/300+ feet/community distances} {Assistance: unassisted/with a cane/with a walker} before requiring rest due to fatigue.

Pt. was examined and Left/Right lower extremity assessment revealed dorsiflexion MMT strength of {MMT Dorsiflexion: 0/1/2/2+/3/3+/4/5}. Plantarflexion MMT strength was {MMT Plantarflexion: 0/1/2/2+/3/3+/4/5/WNL}. Knee extensor strength was {MMT Knee Extensors: 3/3+/4/4+/5}. Passive range of motion to neutral (0° dorsiflexion) is {ROM Neutral: achievable with knee extended/achievable with knee flexed/limited}. Severe fixed equinus deformity is {Fixed Deformity: absent/present} and dynamic fluctuating edema is {Edema: absent/present}. Skin integrity is {Skin Integrity: intact/intact with mild erythema/compromised}.

Gait evaluation reveals {Gait Pattern: steppage gait/slap foot at initial contact/knee hyperextension during stance phase/lack of heel-strike} affecting the Left/Right lower extremity during swing and stance phases.

Due to lower extremity weakness and foot drop with high fall risk, patient requires a dynamic carbon fiber AFO (L1951). Standard polypropylene AFOs are inadequate due to the patient's need for dynamic energy storage and return during stance-to-swing transition to reduce fatigue and stabilize gait. Patient meets all Medicare LCD coverage criteria, including ambulatory status, absence of severe fixed deformity or severe edema, and adequate knee/hip strength to manage dynamic propulsion.

Plan: Fit and adjust HCPCS L1951 (carbon fiber dynamic response AFO) to affected Left/Right lower extremity(ies). Custom modifications to include footplate trimming, heel height alignment, and shoe interface fitting. Patient instructed on donning/doffing, skin monitoring, and footwear requirements. Follow-up scheduled in {Follow-up: 2 weeks/4 weeks}.

cervical-collar.title: Cervical/Trend/Vista
cervical-collar.text:
Patient presented to the North/South clinic for evaluation, fitting, and delivery of a prefabricated rigid cervical orthosis.

Subjective & Medical Rationale:
Patient presents with severe cervical pain and cervical spine instability secondary to {Diagnosis: Cervical Spondylosis / Cervical Radiculopathy / Post-Traumatic Cervical Sprain/Strain / Cervical Disc Displacement / Post-Operative Cervical Fusion / Cervical Fracture / Degenerative Disc Disease of Cervical Spine}. The orthosis is medically necessary to provide rigid multi-planar immobilization (flexion, extension, rotation, and lateral bending), unload cervical vertebrae, facilitate tissue healing, and control movement-induced pain during daily functional activities.

Objective Assessment & Fitting:
Device Fit: Fit with {Brand: Aspen Vista / Trend Medical Rigid Cervical Collar}.

Custom Sizing & Adjustments:
Height adjustment dial/mechanism set to proper anatomical height to maintain the cervical spine in neutral alignment without hyper-extending the chin.  Occipital and mandibular supports contoured and centered to prevent pressure points.  Anterior and posterior sections secured with bilateral hook-and-loop closures to eliminate sagittal/rotational displacement while ensuring uncompromised airway, unobstructed tracheostomy access (if needed), and full swallowing capability.

Functional Assessment & Patient Education:
Immobilization & Fit Verification: Verified cervical motion restriction in sitting and standing positions without excessive impingement on clavicles or mandible.

Donning / Doffing: Patient was instructed on proper neutral alignment, strap sequencing, and donning/doffing procedures. he/she successfully demonstrated independent donning/doffing.

Care & Safety Protocols: Patient was educated  on prescribed wear schedule, pad hygiene/replacement instructions, and skin inspection over bony contact areas (mandible, occiput, sternum, clavicles). {+ Caregiver Present: Caregiver was present and instructed on proper application, neutral positioning during collar changes, and skin checks.}

All questions were answered, and the patient verbalized complete understanding. The orthosis was delivered in proper working condition. Follow-up PRN.

Patient presents to the North/South office for evaluation and anatomical measurement for therapeutic diabetic footwear and total contact inserts. Qualifying Medical History & Rationale:

Therapeutic footwear and inserts are medically necessary to accommodate deformities, relieve shear/friction, redistribute peak plantar pressures, and prevent ulceration or progressive skin breakdown.

Physical Examination & Biomechanical Assessment:

Structural Deformity: Bilateral foot exam reveals {Deformities: no significant rigid deformities / hallux valgus (bunions) / hammer or claw toes / Charcot arthropathy / severe pes planus / prominent metatarsal heads / amputation site}.

{+ Custom Impressions Taken: Direct 3D volumetric impressions / foam impression boxes taken bilaterally for custom-fabricated multi-density inserts (A5513/A5514).}

Plan & Patient Education:
Order Placed: HCPCS A5500 (Pair) and HCPCS {Insert Code: A5512 (Prefab heat-molded, 3 pairs) / A5513 (Custom-molded multi-density, 3 pairs)}.

Next Steps: Patient will return for fitting, in-shoe evaluation, heat-molding/customization, and weight-bearing pressure distribution check upon receipt of order.

Education Provided: Patient was counseled on the break-in schedule (1–2 hours daily with gradual progression), daily visual foot inspections with a mirror, seamless diabetic socks, and immediate reporting of any erythema lasting >20 minutes. {+ Caregiver Present: Caregiver was present and instructed on daily foot inspection and footwear safety.}

Patient was seen at the North/South location for fitting and delivery of a custom-molded Left/Right Solid Ankle-Foot Orthosis (AFO) custom fabricated from patient model with soft interface lining for {Indication: Severe Ankle/Subtalar Instability / Spastic Equinovarus / Drop Foot with Knee Hyperextension / Charcot Neuroarthropathy / Flaccid Paralysis of Lower Extremity/ severe arthritis}.

Clinical Justification:
Patient demonstrates{Diagnosis: severe multidirectional ankle instability/ absent active dorsiflexion and plantarflexion/ spastic tone/extensor thrust/ severe knee instability during stance phase (recurvatum/buckling)} that cannot be controlled with an articulated or flexible device.  {+ Atypical limb size: Pt. has atypical limb shape/size that can only be fit properly with a device that is custom made to his/her shape.}

Technical Fitting & Structural Alignment:
The custom solid AFO was molded to lock the ankle rigidly in {Ankle Position: neutral 90 degrees / 2 degrees dorsiflexion} with rigid anterior/posterior trimlines encompassing the malleoli. Padded tibial strap and instep retention straps adjusted. Shell trimmed and smoothed for comfortable shoe integration. Dynamic gait evaluation confirmed rigid coronal/sagittal plane locking, complete toe clearance in swing phase, and stability of the knee extension moment in stance.

Medical Necessity:
The custom solid AFO is reasonable and medically necessary to eliminate motion in all planes at the ankle and subtalar joints, correct equinovarus deformity, manage ground reaction forces to stabilize the knee during weight-bearing, and allow safe household and community ambulation.

Education & Break-in:
He/she was instructed on a structured break-in schedule (1-2 hours per day initially), proper sock and footwear pairing, and daily skin inspection over the fibular head, navicular, and malleoli. Follow-up PRN in 2-3 weeks.

custom-note-1752097421797.text:
Pt. was seen at the North/South location for custom foot orthotics evaluation. Presents with {Diagnosis: pes planovalgus deformity/plantar fasciitis/heel spur(s)/cavus arches/metatarsal pain/arthritis} in left/right foot/feet.

Custom foot orthotics will help to distribute weight more evenly throughout the heel, longitudinal arches, and transverse arch of the foot.  They will act to help reduce foot/ankle pain help to increase activity levels.  They will also help to provide a more neutral alignment from the ground up through the knees and hips to help reduce long term problems farther up the biomechanical chain.  

Normally wears shoe size {Shoe Size: 4/5/5.5/6/6.5/7/7.5/8/8.5/9/9.5/10/10.5/11/11.5/12/12.5/13/14/15} {Width: B/D/W/XW/XXW/2E/4E/5E/6E/9E}. Impressions were taken today for custom molded functional inserts. Custom functional foot orthotics will be ordered for delivery in 4 weeks.  They will consist of {Support material: Polypro/carbon fiber/soft puff/firm puff/cork} supportive base material with {Top cover: spenco/plastizote/puff/leather/poron/p-cell} top covers, {Heel posting: neutral posting/medial posting/lateral posting}.

F/up 4 weeks for delivery and PRN.

forearm-splint.text: Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of an extended Left/Right forearm and wrist orthosis from {Brand / Manufacturer: Breg / DonJoy / Ossur / DJO / Hely & Weber} for distal radius / forearm fracture / severe tendonitis.
